<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. X.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>VErily, verily, I say unto you, He that entreth not by the door, into the Sheepfold <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">It should seem, that the Sheepfolds in those Countries were Houses which had doors by which the Entry was into them; there is no doubt, but by the <ns0:hi>Sheepfold</ns0:hi> is meant here, The Church of God, in which the People of God are ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thered together in one. By the Door, he apparently mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth himself, as he himself speaketh, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 1. Or rather, more generally that way which God hath appointed for any that are to take charge of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>is Church to enter. He is both the Shepherd, (the true shepherd) and the Door; the <ns0:hi>Shepherd</ns0:hi> as the care, conduct, and Government of the Church belongeth to him, and is upon his shoulders. The <ns0:hi>door,</ns0:hi> as he is he whom the Father hath Ordained to be the Chief Shepherd, from whom all who pretend to any right to Teach, or Govern in the Church, must derive both their Authority and Abilities.</ns0:note>, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Now saith our Saviour, Whoso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ever they be, that thrust themselves into the care, conduct, and government of the Church, without any Call or War<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rant from my Father or Me, who am the true Door through which whosoever entreth into the Church must enter; and the chief Shepherd from whom he must derive, <ns0:hi>or be a Thief and a R<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>bber,</ns0:hi> His very entrance makes it appear, that his end is not to feed the Flock, but to feed himself; and that he drives onely private designe of advantage to himself.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>In this famous Parable which reacheth to</ns0:hi> ver. 31. <ns0:hi>Our Saviour seemeth to drive two great designs.</ns0:hi> 1. <ns0:hi>To prove himself the true Shepherd.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>To prove the Pharisees and Teachers of those times, Thieves, and Robbers.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:350" />2 But he that entreth by the door is the shep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />herd of the sheep <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">As it is amongst men, the true Shepherd goes into the Sheep-fold by the Door; so it is in the Church of God. He that taketh not the honour of governing the Church to himself, but being called of God, as <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> was; he is the <ns0:hi>Shepherd of the sheep</ns0:hi> This very argument the Apostle useth to prove Christ to be the true <ns0:hi>High-Priest, Heb.</ns0:hi> 5.4, 5. Because he <ns0:hi>glorified not himself to be made an High-Priest,</ns0:hi> but was made one by him who said unto him, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110. <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 4. (quoted there also, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 6.) <ns0:hi>Thou art a Priest for ever, after the order of Melchisedeck.</ns0:hi> God (whose the Church is) call'd <ns0:hi>his heritage, his peculiar people,</ns0:hi> &c. was the Door, by which Christ, the chief Shepherd, entred into the Flock; he made him the <ns0:hi>Head of the Church, Ephes.</ns0:hi> 5.23. For this he is said to be <ns0:hi>sent,</ns0:hi> and by often making himself known to us, under the Notion of him whom the Father hath sent. And the under-Shepherds must also derive from Christ, as the <ns0:hi>Fathers will</ns0:hi> in sending. Christ was his Door; So the <ns0:hi>will of Christ</ns0:hi> in sending others, is their <ns0:hi>door</ns0:hi>; that is, their onely true way of entring upon the charge of the Flock of Christ; <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 20.21. <ns0:hi>As my Father hath sent me, so send I you.</ns0:hi> There is a double sending, the one is <ns0:hi>Extraordinary,</ns0:hi> of which mission Christ speaketh to his Apostles in that place; thus the Apostles and first Ministers of the Gospel were sent; Christ breathed upon them, and said, <ns0:hi>Receive you the holy Ghost, Chap.</ns0:hi> 20.22. And there was yet a fuller sending of these first Shepherds, in the days of <ns0:hi>Pentecost, Acts</ns0:hi> 2.17. And there is a more ordinary sending, as to which God revealed his Will, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.2. <ns0:hi>The things that thou hast heard of me amongst many wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others.</ns0:hi> Thus the Apostles, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 14.23. did themselves <ns0:hi>ordain Elders in every Church.</ns0:hi> And <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> for this purpose left <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Creet,</ns0:hi> to set in order <ns0:hi>the things that are wanting, and to ordain Elders in every City.</ns0:hi> Whosoever entreth into any place in the Church, for the feeding and governing of it, that way which God hath directed in his Word, he entreth in by the <ns0:hi>Door,</ns0:hi> he is the <ns0:hi>true Shepherd.</ns0:hi> Concerning Christs Title, and his way of Entrance, and the first Preachers of the Gospel, immediately sent by Christ, and declared to be sent by the Effusion of the Spirit in the days of <ns0:hi>Pentecost</ns0:hi>; there can be no question made by any who believeth the Scriptures of the Old and New Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment. This Text declares, That whosoever cometh into the Church with right, and as a true Shepherd to it, must come in at the <ns0:hi>Door,</ns0:hi> by a Call from God, (as Christ was sent) or from Christ, e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ther by an extraordinary mission, or in such a method an<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> order as Christ hath in his Word directed; either from his own mouth, or by the mouths of his Apostles, whom he ascending up into Heaven, left in the first charge of his Church. This is that which every one ought in the first place to look after. We shall observe in God's whole course with his Church, That in the Corrup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the State of the Church, when it was eminently de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viated from the Rule he had set, he sent some by an extra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ordinary mission: such were the Prophets, whose Writings make up a part of Scripture. Such were the Apostles, and first Ministers of the Gospel. Such we say were our first <ns0:hi>Reformers</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Germany,</ns0:hi> and other parts; nor is it any pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />judice to it, that they were able to work no Miracles; (we read of no Miracles wrought by the Prophets of old, (unless by Two or Three of them.) Their faithful declaring the Will of God, and calling men back to the plain Law of God, in a time when the generality were obviously departed from it, together with their Spirit of courage and boldness in their Work was evident enough, that God had sent them. But this Text onely declareth this general Truth, That every true Shepherd coming into the Church, must come in the right way, by the Door. So the great Shepherd of the Sheep did, being sent by his Father, (whose the Church i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>,) to take care of it; so much all Inferior Shepherds do, by him, whom God the Father hath made the <ns0:hi>Door</ns0:hi>; ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to whose directions all the Affairs of the Church must be ordered.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 To him the porter openeth <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">By the <ns0:hi>Porter</ns0:hi> is understood God; or more particular<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, (to shew the order of the Holy Trinity in working) the <ns0:hi>holy Spirit,</ns0:hi> who openeth the Hearts of men to receive and imbrace Jesus Christ, who is the chief Shepherd;</ns0:note>: and the sheep hear his voice; and he calleth his own sheep by name <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">and the Sheep are able to distinguish his Voice from the Voice of Thieves and Robbers. Probably they had in those Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tries particular Words and Phrases, which their S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>epherds having used their Sheep to, understood, and moved accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to the direction of them. Some think they had al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so Names for their Sheep, (as we have for our Dogs and Horses) which they understood; otherwise, it onely signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fieth, that particular knowledge which Christ hath of all those that are truly his: as the former P<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rase signified, That <ns0:hi>judgment of discerning of Spirits,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Doctrines,</ns0:hi> which was in an eminent degree in the first Ministers of the Gospel<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and is yet in a measure in Believers; by which tho they cannot perfectly and infallibly judge concerning Truth, and the Will of God, in all things; yet they can in a great measure do it, and are not ordinarily led aside into pernici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and damnable Errours<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to the ruine of their Souls.</ns0:note>, and leadeth them out <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And saith our Saviour, the true Shepherd <ns0:hi>leadeth the sheep out</ns0:hi>; that is, into their Pastures and true feeding-places. This is eminently true concerning Christ the chief Shepherd; when he came into the World, God open<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to him the Door of his Church; so as tho he was re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jected by many, (the Builders and Rulers of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Church</ns0:hi> in particular:) yet he was by many received, multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tudes followed him; many truly believed on him, and tru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly heard his Voice, he had a particular knowledge of them, who truly were his Sheep: he knew <ns0:hi>Nathaniel</ns0:hi> while he was yet under the Fig-tree. He led them out into their true Pastures, Preaching the Gospel of the Kingdome to them, and shewing them the way of Life and Salvation. It is in its measure true of every inferior Shepherd, that truly deriveth from Christ; God giveth unto such, favour in the eyes of his People. The true Sheep of Christ, hear them, receive, and imbrace the Truth delivered by them. They take a particular charge of them, and they <ns0:hi>lead</ns0:hi> them to Christ, and to the imbracing of his Gospel; as by the ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly and true Doctrine which they Preach to them, so by their holy Lives and Conversations before them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                     <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> 
                  <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>heep follow him <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">In our Countrey at <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, Shepherds generally fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low their Sheep, which go before them. In other Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tries, as <ns0:hi>France, &c.</ns0:hi> it is otherwise at this day, the Shep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />herds go before their Flocks, and their Flocks follow them, upon some sounds they make. In <ns0:hi>Palestina,</ns0:hi> (which was the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> Country) it should seem, that the Shepherds sometimes went before their Sheep, and sometimes followed them. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> followed his Fathers Sheep, 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 7.8. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 78.71. On the other side, God is spoken of, <ns0:hi>Psal</ns0:hi> 80 1. under the Notion of the <ns0:hi>Shepherd of Israel, who leadest Ioseph like a flock.</ns0:hi> And the <ns0:hi>Psalmist, Psal</ns0:hi> 23.1. speaking of God as his Shepherd, saith, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Thou leadest me beside the still waters.</ns0:hi> Christ here speaketh of himself under the Notion of a Shepherd that went before his Sheep, and whom the Sheep followed; and thereby lets us know the duty of all faithful Pastors in the Church, so to live, that their Flocks may follow them with safety; which cannot be, unless they follow Christ, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.1.</ns0:note>, for they know his voice<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">For saith our Saviour, Those that are my true Sheep, they know <ns0:hi>my voice</ns0:hi>; thereby signifying, that power of discerning betwixt Tru<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>h and damnable Errors, which the Lord gives unto all tr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Believers, 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2.27.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And a stranger will they not follow, but <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                     <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> flee from him: for they know not the voice <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                     <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> strangers <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">This he further enlargeth upon, telling them, That his Sheep would not follow those that did not lead them into his Truth, and in his ways, for they understood not such Voices. Here ariseth a Question; <ns0:hi>Whether the Elect of God,</ns0:hi> or such as being <ns0:hi>truly called,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>believe in Christ,</ns0:hi> are <ns0:hi>the Sheep of Christ</ns0:hi> in the most strict and proper sense, may not be seduced into Errors, and led away by Strangers? <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> We must distinguish first, betwixt single persons, and the generality of Believers: As in a Flock, the generality keep together, following the Voice of the true Shepherd; tho some particular Sheep may wander: So the generality of Believers will be found keeping close to the Truth and Doctrine of Christ, tho amongst them some particular per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons may be seduced, and led a way by Seducers. Secondly, we must distinguish <ns0:hi>betwixt Errors,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>damnable Errors,</ns0:hi> a pertinacious adherence to which, will divide the Soul from Christ, and end in the ruine of Souls. Christs Sheep may follow strangers, dissembling the Spiritual Voice of the true Shepherd a little way, but they will not follow them into such Errors as will plunge their Souls in Eternal Ruine and Destruction. Thirdly, They may hear even this Voice of but Strangers speaking to them perverse and damnable things: but it will be but for a short time, God will reduce, and bring them back again, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 28. <ns0:hi>They shall never perish.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:350" />6 This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spake unto them <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Our Saviour was wont to instruct them in the Myste<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ries of the Kingdom of God by <ns0:hi>Parables</ns0:hi>; that is, <ns0:hi>Similitudes</ns0:hi> taken from reasonable actions of men, which might be, and were proper to express Spiritual things by: wherefore he used this Method in Teaching, we are told, <ns0:hi>Matth</ns0:hi> 13, 10, 11, 12, 13. They well enough understood the words in which those Parables were delivered; but the Inward Sense, the Spiritual Mysteries shadowed out in those Similitudes: these they understood not, neither the common sort of his Disciples understood them, nor did the better sort of his Disciples understand them, without a further explication of them. Our Lord therefore in the following verses, comes to give them a large explication of the Parable.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily verily I say unto you, I am the door of the Sheep <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Our Saviour had before been speaking of the Door in another Notion; there he spake of the <ns0:hi>door of the Shepherd,</ns0:hi> here of the <ns0:hi>door of the Sheep</ns0:hi>; there of the Door (that is) the true and regular way of Entrance into the Care, Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duct, and Government of the Church: here, of the true way of Entrance, not into the Church Militant onely, but into the Church Triumphant. It may be also understood of the Door, or way of Entrance and admission into the Church Visible here upon the Earth. <ns0:hi>Circumcision, Baptism, External Profession,</ns0:hi> are the Doors into the <ns0:hi>Visible Church</ns0:hi>; but none unless by Christ, that is, by a true and lively Faith wrought by the Spirit of Christ in the Soul, can be a true Member of Christs <ns0:hi>Invisible Church</ns0:hi> here upon the Earth, much less a Member of his <ns0:hi>Glorious Church</ns0:hi> in Heaven.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 All that ever came before me, are thieves, and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">This must not be understood of the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> but of such onely as came before Christ, not being sent by him; all those that taught people another way of Life and Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation, than by believing in the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> who was to be Revealed for the Salvation of the World: all such did but seek themselves, not the good of peoples Souls, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroyed Souls instead of profiting, or doing them any good. But those that were mine by an External Election, or by my special Grace bestowed upon them, did not imbrace them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hap. 14.6.</ns0:note> I am the door, by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Our Saviour here lets us know, that he meant by the Door in, the former <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> the Door of Salvation; the way by which every man must enter into Life, that findeth Life; not the <ns0:hi>door</ns0:hi> onely by which every true Pastor must enter in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to the Church, but by which every Soul that shall be saved, must enter into Heaven; which is the Doctrine which he before taught, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.16, 18, 36.</ns0:note>, and shall go in and out, and find pasture <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">And he, who so be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieveth in me, shall be so guided, and govern'd, and <ns0:hi>taught,</ns0:hi> that he shall be secure, and want nothing for the managery of his whole conversation in the World. Under the Notion of <ns0:hi>Pasture</ns0:hi> here, are signified all good things that the Soul can stand in need of: It is much the same promise with that <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 6.35. <ns0:hi>He that cometh to me, shall never hunger; and he that believeth in me, shall never thirst.</ns0:hi> And with that <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 84.11. as also with the 23 <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi>; to which <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> our Saviour is thought in this Parable to have a special reference.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 The thief cometh not but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Look as it is with the true Shepherd, that owneth the Sheep, and whose the Flock is; he cometh regularly into the care and conduct of it; he cometh into the Sheep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fold, to take care of the Life, and welfare of his Sheep; but a Thief, and a Robber, that climbeth into the Win<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dow, and so gets into the Sheepfold, he comes not there out of any good-will to the Sheep, but meerly by destroy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Sheep, to provide for himself: So it is with them that without any Call, or derivation of Authority from me, thrust themselves into the care and conduct of the Church of God, they do it with no good Design to the Souls of peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, not out of any care or respect unto their good; but meerly that they may serve themselves in the ruine of my peoples Souls.</ns0:note>: I am come that they might have life <ns0:hi>r,</ns0:hi> and that they might have it more abun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dantly <ns0:hi>s.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">But that is not my end, in coming into the World: I am not come to Destroy them, but to save them; I am come, that they might have a Spiritual Life, and at last, Eternal Life; that they might live the Life of Grace here, and not fail of the Life of Glory hereafter; and not onely that they may barely live, but that their life may abound, through the upholdings, strengthnings, quick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nings, and comfortings of my holy and gracious Spirit. That my Beloved may not onely drink, but <ns0:hi>drink abundantly</ns0:hi>; not onely live, but live abundantly furnished with all the affluences and accomodations of a Spiritual Life.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 34.23<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> & 37.24. Heb. 13.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1 Pet. 5.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> I am the good Shepherd: The good Shep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />herd giveth his life for the sheep <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>That good Shepherd,</ns0:hi> Prophecied of, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.11. I can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not agree with those who think, that Christ here speaketh not of himself as the <ns0:hi>good Shepherd,</ns0:hi> with reference to his Office, as he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; but onely in opposition to the <ns0:hi>Hirelings</ns0:hi> after mentioned. I can allow, that he thus cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />leth himself, both in the one respect, and the other; but I cannot allow the latter sense exclusively to the former; for what followeth, is peculiar to the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> of whom it was Prophecied, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.26. <ns0:hi>That he should be cut off, but not for himself</ns0:hi>: and though it be true, That the <ns0:hi>true shepherd</ns0:hi> will hazard his Life for his Sheep, as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> did, when he encountred the Lion, and the Bear, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 17, 34, 35. yet it cannot be said to be the duty of the best Shepherd, to lay down his Life for the Sheep; for the life of a Man is much more valuable than the Life of any Beast. Our Saviour therefore doubtless in this place sheweth wherein he was the most excellent Shepherd, far excelling the best Shepherds in the World, because he was come, not onely to expose, hazard, and adventure his Life; but actually, willingly, and freely to lay it down.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Those that deal in Sheep, either keep them themselves, or by their near Relations, as <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> Sons, and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Labans</ns0:hi> Daughters did; or else they hired persons to keep them for them. There is a great deal of difference be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt the care of an owner, and the care of an hired Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vant in any thing; The owner taketh a more Natural dili<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gent care, because the whole profit of the Sheep, thriving, and doing well, returneth unto himself. The hired Servant may be careful in his measure, and degree; but no such Servant will take the care that an Owner will take; nor run the hazards that he will run, because he knoweth, that let the Flock thrive never so well, he shall have no more than the Wages he is hired for: therefore, what our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our saith, is true, concerning the generality of such hired Servants, they will take some care of the Flocks of Sheep in their trust, so long as there appeareth no danger; but if any danger appeareth, they leave the Sheep, and flee, and the Wolf cometh, and scattereth the Sheep.</ns0:note>, seeth the wolf coming, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zech 11.16 17.</ns0:note> leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scatter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth the sheep.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 The hireling fleeth, because he is an hire<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling, and careth not for the Sheep <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The reason why, he that is a meer hired Servant, and hath no property in the Sheep, fleeth, is, because he is an Hireling, and doth what lie doth meerly for his Wages; and when a danger ariseth, which <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>is Wages will not ballance, he will never encounter it, he hath no property in the Sheep, nor any love to them, nor care of them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 I am the good Shepherd, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Tim. 2.19.</ns0:note> know my <ns0:hi>sheep,</ns0:hi> and am known of mine <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">I am no Hireling, the sheep are mine own, I have a true love and affection for them, which obligeth me to a just and true care of them; I know them by Name, (as was said before) by a particular distinct knowledge; or I love them, and have tender bowels for them; and as I know them, so I am mutually known, and owned, and acknowledg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed by them; they have heard my voice, and discerned be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt my voice, and the voice of such as are strangers, re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fusing to follow them; but following me, going before them. Thus our Saviour in the same Parable giveth us both notes to know a true, and good Shepherd, and particularly to know that himself was the true, good, and most excel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lent Shepherd: and also Notes, by which we might know who they are that are the true Sheep of Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 11.27.</ns0:note> As the Father knoweth me, even so know my Father <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">By these words our Saviour openeth, How he knew his sheep, and should be again known of them, even as the Father knoweth him, and he knows his Father: this mutu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />al knowledge between the Father and Christ, was joyned with perfect love and delight. Thus our Saviour knoweth those that are his sheep, not onely fully and distinctly, so as to call them all by their Names; but so as to love them, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />light in them, so as to be ready to lay down his Life for their good, and Eternal Salvation. Christ, to shew not one<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly the sincerity, but the Degrees of his love to his people, doth often compare it to the love wherewith <ns0:hi>his father loved him, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 15.9 and <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 17.23, 26. So that if we can believe, That God the Father loved Christ his onely begotten So<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, we may also believe, That both the Fath<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r and Christ love those that are truly the sheep of Chris<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. The love that Christ hath to his People is as true, and as certain as the Fathers love to Christ, or Christs love to his Father; and this could be shewed by no higher act, tha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> that of laying down his Life, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 15.13. <ns0:hi>Now,</ns0:hi> saith he, <ns0:hi>I lay down</ns0:hi>; that is, I am ready to lay down, or I shall short<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly lay down my life for the sheep; whether <ns0:hi>Sheep</ns0:hi> can sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifie all, and every person born into the World, is their con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cern more strictly to enquire, who are so <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>enacious of that point, That Christ died equally for All, and Every man; As also, whether upon that Principle that absurdity must not follow, That Christ loved those who shall yet perish Eternally, with such a love as the Father loved him, and he loved the Father.</ns0:note>, and I lay down my life for the sheep <ns0:hi>z.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:351" />16 And other sheep I have which are not of this fold <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Our Saviour meaneth the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> who belonged not to the <ns0:hi>Iewish State</ns0:hi> and Church, so were not under the same Laws and Government; for 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2.2. he was not onely a Propitiation for the Sins of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> but for the Sins of the whole World; he calleth those sheep, because the Lord knew who were his from Eternity; and they were sheep in the councils of God, and they were suddenly to be made his sheep by Calling, the Gospel being soon to be Preached to all Nations.</ns0:note>: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Them also, (saith he) <ns0:hi>I must bring in.</ns0:hi> It is so written in God's Book, the Promises, and Prophecies to that purpose must be fulfilled. They shall not onely hear the Voice and Sound of my Gospel, though go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing out of <ns0:hi>Sion,</ns0:hi> yet not terminated in <ns0:hi>Sion</ns0:hi>; but they shall imbrace, receive, and believe that joyful sound.</ns0:note>; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 37.22.</ns0:note> and there shall be one fold, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> one shepherd <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">And there shall be but one Church; as I am one Shepherd, so there shall be but one Flock of sheep; one Body, one Spirit, one hope of our Calling, one Lord, one Faith; one Baptism, as there is one God and Father of All, as the <ns0:hi>Apostle</ns0:hi> speaketh, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 4.4, 5, 7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Therefore doth my father love me, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 53.7, 8, 12.</ns0:note> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause I lay down my life, that I may take it again <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Christ here asserteth Two things. 1. That he was about to lay down his life, and should now very shortly lay it down; but yet so, as he should take it again. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> rise again from the Dead, Death should not have Dominion over him; by which he comforteth his Disciples concerning his Death, declaring, 1. That he was a <ns0:hi>Freewill-Offering,</ns0:hi> as he further openeth it in the next Verse. 2. That he should not perish in the Grave, but rise again from the Dead. 2. That therefore the Father loved him; for by this means he declared himself with power to be the Son of God, and the Father could not but love his Son. And 2. By this means also he humbled himself, and became obedient unto Death; even the Death upon the Cross, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.8. So as that the Father had many reasons to love the Son, so amongst others this obedience of his to Death, even the accursed Death upon the Cross, to fulfill his Fathers Will, for the Redemp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion and Salvation of the Sons of Men, was not the least: and by this also he commendeth his Fathers love to those that are his sheep, in that his Father loveth him with the more exceeding love, for laying down his Life, to purchase their Redemption, and Salvation.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 No man taketh it from m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>, but I lay it down of my self: I have power to lay it down, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.19. Act. 2.24.</ns0:note> I have power to take it again <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">No man taketh it from me by force, without my wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling it, and consenting to it; the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pilate</ns0:hi> will take it from me, but not without my free and voluntary surren<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der of it; and this is that which we read, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 4.27, 28. <ns0:hi>For of a truth, against thy holy child Iesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilat, and the Gentiles, with the people of Israel, were gathered together, for to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel had determined before to be done,</ns0:hi> &c. By which he asserteth his Divine power, and so comforteth his Disciples against the disturbances they were like to have from the sight of his Passion, at this time not many Months of. And this (saith he)</ns0:note>. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.19. Act. 2.24.</ns0:note> This commandment have I received of my Father <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">is the Will of my Father, that which my Father hath given me Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mission to do, and for which he hath sent me into the World: And thus he declareth his Death to be a fulfilling of his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers purpose, and an act of Obedience to his Fathers Will; and indeed, in his Obedience in the thing, lay much of the vertue of his Death.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 There was a division therefore again amongst the Jews for these sayings <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Christ by his Words often caused a Division amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> so as they could not agree in their sentiments, and censures about him; which was either caused through the mixture amongst them, of such as truly Believed, with those which Believed not. Or else from the mixture of a more considering part amongst them, with others which were more Brutish, Irrational, and full of Passion. We met with much the same, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 7.43. and again, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 9.16. It is one Method of God's Providence for the deliverance of his Servants from unreasonable men, to cause divisions among them; so as they cannot agree among themselves.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And many of them said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.20 & 8.48, 52.</ns0:note> He hath a devil, and is mad, why hear ye him <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Some of the People said, <ns0:hi>He had a Devil, and was mad.</ns0:hi> For (as was said before) this was the Opinion of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> concerning all that were Mad, and Destracted, That it was by the Influence of the Devil, and they were infested with an Evil Spirit.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Others said, these are not the words of him that hath a devil <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">But others that were less Passionate and Brutish in their Expressions, and more thinking, and considerate in passing their judgments, said, These are not the <ns0:hi>words</ns0:hi> (so we translate it; the word in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which signifies <ns0:hi>things,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>matters,</ns0:hi> as well as Words; and by what follows, one would think that were the more proper Translation of it here) they instance in no words, but in a matter of Fact. Asking, if a Devil could open the Eyes of the Blind? that is, of one that was born Blind: for they certainly speak with reference to that Miracle which he had so lately wrought upon such a person.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 4.11. Psal. 146.8.</ns0:note> Can a Devil <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.6, 7.</ns0:note> open the eyes of the blind?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And it was at Hierusalem, the feast of the dedication, and it was winter <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:p>This Verse affords Two Questions, which have not a little troubled Interpreters. 1. <ns0:hi>What feast of Dedication this was.</ns0:hi> 2. Whether <ns0:hi>Dedications of places to the Worship of God be warrantable, or no,</ns0:hi> in that manner as they are Dedicated amongst the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> at this day. As to the first of these, That which we have about it in Scripture is this, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 40. from the First to the Fifteenth Verse, we have Gods Command and Direction for the <ns0:hi>Hallowing,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Dedica<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Sanctuary,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Tabernacle,</ns0:hi> which was the first House we read of in Scripture, set apart for the Publick Worship of God. We have a particular accompt of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> his punctual Obedience to that Command, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 8. When the Temple was Builded by <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> we read of <ns0:hi>Solomons</ns0:hi> Dedication of it; but nothing of Ceremony used at it, one<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly a Multitude of <ns0:hi>Sacrifices</ns0:hi> Offered, (which was God's or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinary Worship in the <ns0:hi>Iewish Church,</ns0:hi>) and a Feast kept Fourteen days: We read of no Law that he made for the <ns0:hi>Annual</ns0:hi> keeping of it: no Obligation upon all the Males in <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> to be present at it: As concerning the other So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lemn Feasts which God appointed, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 33. and <ns0:hi>Solomons Feast of Dedication</ns0:hi> in this differed from them, that it held double the time, for Seven, or Eight days was the longest time that any of those Feasts were kept. This Temple was Destroy'd by the <ns0:hi>Caldeans,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Babylonians</ns0:hi>; and Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />builded by <ns0:hi>Zorobabel, Ezra,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Nehemiah,</ns0:hi> as we read in the Books known by that Name. In <ns0:hi>Analogy</ns0:hi> to the practice of <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> when they had finished the Building of the Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, there was another <ns0:hi>Feast</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Dedication</ns0:hi> kept; of which we read, <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> 6.16, 17, 18. but we read of nothing done in that Dedication, but the offering of 100 Bullocks, 200 Rams, 400 Lambs, and 12 He-Goats; and setting the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> in order for the service of God. This Temple was defaced by <ns0:hi>Antiochus,</ns0:hi> but not wholly ruin'd; and was Repaired and Purifyed by <ns0:hi>Iudas Maccabeus,</ns0:hi> of which we read, 2 <ns0:hi>Maccab.</ns0:hi> 2.23. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10 6, 7, 8. 1 <ns0:hi>Maccab.</ns0:hi> 4.52, 58. which Books of <ns0:hi>Maccabes,</ns0:hi> though they be no <ns0:hi>Canonical Scripture,</ns0:hi> yet are as good a piece of <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical History</ns0:hi> as any; and <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> also giveth us an account of it, <ns0:hi>Antiq. l.</ns0:hi> 12. <ns0:hi>cap.</ns0:hi> 11. We do not read of any thing they did, saving Offering <ns0:hi>Sacrifices,</ns0:hi> and setting things in order, according to the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and Feasting; <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> tells us, They <ns0:hi>used all Lawful Pleasures.</ns0:hi> We do not read, that either God appointed an <ns0:hi>Annual</ns0:hi> Feast of <ns0:hi>Dedication</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Sanctuary,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Ezra,</ns0:hi> for either of the <ns0:hi>Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples:</ns0:hi> but we read twice in the Book of <ns0:hi>Machabes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sephus</ns0:hi> (Writing the <ns0:hi>Iewish History</ns0:hi> tells us,) That <ns0:hi>Iudas Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chabeus</ns0:hi> made it a Law, That the Feast should be kept Yearly for Eight Days, in Memory of that Mercy which God had shewed them. This was without doubt the <ns0:hi>Feast of Dedication</ns0:hi> here mentioned: for this Feast began upon the Twenty fifth day of the Moneth <ns0:hi>Chisleu,</ns0:hi> which answereth our Moneths of <ns0:hi>November</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>December,</ns0:hi> and took in part of each; so it agreeth with the Text which saith, <ns0:hi>That it was in Winter:</ns0:hi> whereas <ns0:hi>Solomons</ns0:hi> Dedication was in <ns0:hi>Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tumn, Ezra's</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Spring.</ns0:hi> Some make a Question, Whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:hi>Iudas Machabeus</ns0:hi> did well in appointing this <ns0:hi>Annual</ns0:hi> Feast; neither <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> having, that we read of be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, done any such thing: and that our Saviour was not at this Feast in any honour to the Feast, but onely to take advantage of the Multitude of People that met to Preach the Gospel. For my own part, as I will not defend, so I durst not condemn him: I see no more that he did in this, than was done <ns0:hi>Esth.</ns0:hi> 9.27, 28. as to the days of <ns0:hi>Purim.</ns0:hi> Magi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strates certainly have a power to appoint Publick days, yea <ns0:hi>Annual</ns0:hi> days of Thanksgivings, for Mercies never to be for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gotten. Indeed they cannot make a day holy, so as it shall be a sin against God to labour in it, or to use any plea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sures (as in the case of the Sabbath) but they may command the publick Worship of God to be performed on particular days, and men ought to attend it when with conveniency they can: Onely they ought to take care that such days be not spent in Luxury and Profaneness, and that they be for signal Providences, and not so multiplyed, and frequently renewing, as that the service of them degenerate into meer matter of form. Whether Christ went up in order to the Feast, or because of the great concourse of people he knew would be there at that time, cannot be determined.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p>For the second Question, It is not so much a question, whether it be lawful in a solemn and decent manner, to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />secrate an house to the publick Worship of God, by such Acts of Worship as God hath appointed under the Gospel; such as Prayer and Praise, Reading, Preaching and hearing the Word: As whether it may be done by such Rites and Ceremonies as the Papists do it with, for the which there is no institution; for the former, though it may be some will not agree it necessary; yet certainly, no sober person can deny, but if a place be made for people ordinarily to meet in to Worship God, there, they may as well meet at the first to Praise God for his mercy, and to beg his presence, when they shall there meet together to Worship God, and to hear his Word, as they may meet there afterwards for Prayer, Praise, Preaching; or Hearing; but this satisfieth not the Papists. They first do it by many Superstitious Ceremo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nies. Secondly, They plead for the Holiness of the place when so Consecrated. As the Ceremonies of their <ns0:hi>Consecra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions,</ns0:hi> or Dedications. <ns0:hi>Bellarmine</ns0:hi> reckoneth up eight.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="1">1. The <ns0:hi>Painting</ns0:hi> twelve Crosses in the several parts of the house to be Consecrated, and lighting up twelve Lamps, one at every Cross; To signifie the twelve Apostles who carried the Banner of the Cross throughout the world.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="2">2. The Bishop's knocking at the door with a Pastoral staff, commanding the Devil to give place, and invoking of God, the Angels and Saints, to grant their presence in that place, which they make to signifie the opening of peoples hearts by the Preaching of the Gospel.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="3">3. The scattering of ashes upon the flore of the places, upon which the <ns0:hi>Bishop</ns0:hi> writes the letters of the <ns0:hi>Latine</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Greek <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> in the figure of a Cross.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="4">4. The sprinkling the place with Holy-water, and lighting up wax Candles.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="5">5. The <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> of the Crosses before mentioned, and painted on the walls.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="6">6. The sprinkling of the place, with a mixture of Water, Wine, Salt, and Ashes.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="7">7. The anointing of the Temple, and the Altar.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="8">8. The keeping of a Festival upon it: And for all these they have devised several significancies too vain and fanci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful to repeat.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p>For none of which we know not the least warrant in holy writ: Nor can we conceive, how any Consecration can im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />print any character of holiness upon a place, or make pray<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers offered up in or toward it more acceptable: though we know it did so as to the Temple, both because it was an emi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nent Type of Christ, and also because of the particular pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mises made to it, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 9. which were not applicable to the <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> which were the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> ordinary meeting-pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces for publick Worship, but onely to the Temple upon the account before mentioned. Tho we say that all places for that use, ought to be used with all imaginable decency; and we ought during the publick Worship of God, to carry our selves in them with all reverence, because of the Angels, and because of the special presence of God, promised to the assemblies of his people in his name, and for his publick Worship.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:351" />23 And Jesus walked in the Temple <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 3.11. and 5.12.</ns0:note> in So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lomons porch <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Of this <ns0:hi>Solomons porch</ns0:hi> we read, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 6.3. that <ns0:hi>Solo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon built the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits long, and ten cubits broad.</ns0:hi> This was the place where they walked in winter, though this was destroyed when <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem</ns0:hi> was destroyed by the <ns0:hi>Babylonians</ns0:hi>; yet it seemeth that there was one builded that was like it, and kept that name. It should seem that it was a place better defended from the weather, then those other parts of the Temple where in Summer-time they used to walk</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long doest thou <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or hold us is su<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>pence.</ns0:note> make us to doubt? If thou be the Christ tell us plain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Our Saviour was at this time within three months of his Crucifying; he had often before told them that he was the <ns0:hi>light of the world,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>true Shepherd,</ns0:hi> he had Preached Doctrine to them, from whence they might easily have con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cluded what he was; he had wrought works among them which none could do but by a Divine Power; but he had been very wary of telling them in plain terms that he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>; when at any time he had so decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red himself to his Disciples, or they had owned him as such, he s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ill laid a charge upon them, to tell no man of it, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.20, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> They therefore come to him, demanding a plain resolution in the case; some of their minds were in some sus<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pence about it. It was but a captious question, for had he denied it, besides that, it had been the denial of a truth which he came to bear a testimony unto; they had had a great ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vantage to have lessened his reputation amongst those who had believed on him as such. Had he affirmed it, he had brought himself in danger of the <ns0:hi>Roman Governor,</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> indeed expected a <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> but to be a <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poral Prince,</ns0:hi> to deliver them from their Enemies; and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or him to have declared himself such a Christ, as they expected, had been fatal to them. He therefore answers with his usual prudence and wariness to this question.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Jesus answered them. I told you, and ye believed not <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">I have in effect told it you more than once; I have told you, that I am sent of the Father, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> I have said enough for you to conclude it; but you will not understand, you will not receive it, you will not believe what I say.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.36. Ver. 38.</ns0:note> Name <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">What need you any further witness of it, than those works which I do by Divine Power? by vertue of my oneness with my Father, and of that Power and Authority which he hath committed to me, that by them I might confirm the Doctrine which I have taught you.</ns0:note>, they bear witness of me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.47.</ns0:note> ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as I said unto you <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Acts 13.48. <ns0:hi>As many as were ordained to life, believed.</ns0:hi> Here our Saviour giveth this as one reason of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />belief, that they <ns0:hi>were not of his sheep</ns0:hi>; were they not <ns0:hi>Isra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />elites?</ns0:hi> yes, but all are not <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> that are descended of <ns0:hi>Isra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />el.</ns0:hi> It seems a very hard interpretation that some would put upon these words; <ns0:hi>ye believe not, because you are not teach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />able, and fit to be made my sheep,</ns0:hi> the words are <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Nor can such interpretation be paralelled from any other Scripture. That by <ns0:hi>sheep,</ns0:hi> here, cannot be meant members of the Church, is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>; for they were of the <ns0:hi>Church of Israel,</ns0:hi> whom the Lord led as a stock, (as the <ns0:hi>Psalmist</ns0:hi> speaks, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 80.1.) That <ns0:hi>Believers,</ns0:hi> and such as are truly called and sanctified, are not meant, is as plain; for then the sense would be, <ns0:hi>you believe not, because you believe not</ns0:hi>; besides, our Saviour had be<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> said, <ns0:hi>He had other sheep that were not of that fold,</ns0:hi> (by which he meant the Gentiles) such, for whom he prayed, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 17.20. being such <ns0:hi>as should believe on him</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>sheep</ns0:hi> therefore he meaneth, certainly, such as were <ns0:hi>ordained to life,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 13. 48. Nor will it therefore follow, that Gods not ordination of them to life, was the near and immediate <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of their not believing; but their own stubborn, and perverse wills in not <ns0:hi>repenting, that they might believe.</ns0:hi> As our Saviour tells them, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.32. that is, not turning from their gross and sinful ways, which they might have done by vertue of that common grace of God, which was afforded them in the Gospel, by the Preaching of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> and of <ns0:hi>Christ himself.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This is the same which he said <ns0:hi>verse</ns0:hi> 4. (see the notes there).</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And I give unto them eternal life, <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">I do give them, and I will give them eternal life; as soon as they shall come to hear, and believe my voice, and to fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low me, they shall have a sure right and title to it; and when my Father by his Providence shall remove them out of the world, and in the great day, they shall be taken up into the actual possession of it.</ns0:note> and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 21. and 18.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> they shall never perish <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">For they shall never perish, but though they may fall, they shall<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> rise again by repen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance.</ns0:note>, neither shall any pluck them out of my hand <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">They are in my hand, and my hand shall preserve them, none shall ever pluck them out of it; they shall be preserved through faith, by the Power of God to eternal life and Salvation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 14:2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> My Father which gave <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> me, is greater than all <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">All that are my sheep, became so by my Fathers dona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion and gift; so as my Father is equally with my self con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerned in the preservation of them to that happy end, to which he hath ordained and designed them. Those that would pluck them out of my hand, and deprive them of that eternal life which I will give them, must be too strong, not for me alone, but for my Father also, which none is, for who can be too strong for Omnipotence?</ns0:note>: and no man is able to pluck <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> out of my Fathers hand.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 I and <ns0:hi>my</ns0:hi> Father are one <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">My Father and I are one, not only in <ns0:hi>Counsel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Will,</ns0:hi> (as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 17.11, 12. And believers are said to be of one heart, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 4.32.) but in Nature, Power, and Essence; for it is plain, that our Saviour here ascribeth the preservation of his sheep, not to the Will, but to the Power of his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther. <ns0:hi>None is able to pluck them out of my Fathers hand.</ns0:hi> And it is plain by what followes, that the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> thus under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood our Saviour: Some eminent <ns0:hi>Protestant</ns0:hi> Interpreters expound this of an <ns0:hi>oneness</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Consent</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Will,</ns0:hi> doing the same things, and driving the same design; both agreeing to pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serve the Sheep unto Eternal Life; but (with all respect un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to them) I think the context implieth more, though this be not excluded.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:352" />31 Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Tumultuously, as we read they did once before, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 8.59. From whence we may learn with what design they came to Christ, ver. 24. plainly to tell them whether he were the Christ. By the Law of God the false Prophet was to be stoned; but he was first to be judicially tryed, and Judged: This was but a Tumultuous action of an inraged Multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Jesus answered them, Many good works have I shewed you from my Father: for which of those works do you stone me <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The word Translated good, is of a very large significa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; signifying, Excellent, Useful, Profitable, Beauteous, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Whatsoever in common speech cometh under the No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of Good: I (saith our Saviour) never did harm to any of you, but I have been the Instrument of a great deal of good to you. I have given sight to the Blind, hearing to the Deaf, healed many that were Sick of grievous diseases, cast out many Devils out of those which were infested with, or possessed by them. Do any of these deserve any such usage at your hands? What maketh you in such a rage a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst me?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone thee not, <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">These are not the things we are incensed against thee for; we grant that thou hast done many good Works a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst us; these we gratefully acknowledg.</ns0:note> but for blasphemy, and because that thou being a man, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.18.</ns0:note> makest thy self God <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">But this is that which we are not able to bear, That whereas thou art but a meer man, by thy discourses thou makest thy self equal with God, and so art guilty of <ns0:hi>Blasphemy,</ns0:hi> which is committed as well by arrogating to our selves what is pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per to God, as by imputing to God the Natural or Moral imperfections of the Creature; and the Blasphemer deser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veth to be stoned, according to the Law of God. By this it is manifest, that the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> understood our Saviour, affirming that He and his Father were One; as asserting himself <ns0:hi>One in Essenee</ns0:hi> with his Father, not in <ns0:hi>Will</ns0:hi> onely.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">This was written, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 82.6. The whole Scripture of the Old Testament, being wrote by holy Men, inspired of God, and ditective of mens Conversation before men, and towards God, is sometimes call'd <ns0:hi>The Law, Psal.</ns0:hi> 19.7. It was spoken concerning <ns0:hi>Magistrates,</ns0:hi> and the Governors of Gods People, who being Gods Deputies, and Vicegerents, intrusted to execute the Judgments and Vengeance of God, and Dignified with the name of gods.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">If God Dignified those Men, (and many of them were also vile and Sinful Men) with the Title of gods, because they had a Commission to Govern People according to the Law of God</ns0:note>, and the scripture cannot be bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">and none must contradict what God hath said in his word; there can be no falshood in the Revelation of any part of the Divine will.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Say ye of him <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.27.</ns0:note> whom the Father hath sanctified and sent into the world <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Suppose I were no more then a meer man, yet being <ns0:hi>Sanctified,</ns0:hi> that is, set apart of God for the special work of Mans Redemption; and sent of God into the World, with Commission both to reveal and to do his Will; yet dare you say, that I <ns0:hi>blaspheme,</ns0:hi> because I said, <ns0:hi>I am the Son of God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, Thou blas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phemest <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.17, 18.</ns0:note>: because I said <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 1.35.</ns0:note>, I am the Son of God <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">In the place, <ns0:hi>viz Psal.</ns0:hi> 82.6. Where God said of Magi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strates, <ns0:hi>ye are gods</ns0:hi>; He also added, <ns0:hi>all of you are Children of the most High</ns0:hi>; you have therefore no reason to rage at me, though I did say I was the Son of God; being one whom the Father hath in his Eternal Counsels set apart for this great and special Work; and actually by his Providence sent into the World for the finishing and dispatching of it. But we must take heed, that we do not understand our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour here, as if he in another sense assumed to him the Title of the Son of God; it was enough for him at present to assert, that the Title well enough belonged to him, if he indeed had been no more than the <ns0:hi>Son of Man,</ns0:hi> as they said.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> If I do not the works of my Father, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve me not <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Our Saviour doth often appeal to his Works to testifie concerning his Divine Mission and Power: These works, he here calleth <ns0:hi>the works of his Father</ns0:hi>; by which he doth not onely mean works that are pleasing and acceptable to God, as acts of Obedience to the Will of God, performed by Men, may be called, and are, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.28, 29. nor (as I conceive) onely those works which he did by Commission and Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority from his Father; which <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 17.4. He calleth <ns0:hi>the work which his Father had given him to do.</ns0:hi> But those works which none but God could do; such were the multiplication of the loaves, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.11, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> The curing of him who was <ns0:hi>born blind, Chap.</ns0:hi> 9.41, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> If (saith our Saviour) I do not do those works which no meer Man ever did, give me no credit; but if I do those works, which can be done by no humane Art or Power, you have reason to believe me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 But If I do, though ye believe not me <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">If I do such works as can be done by no less than a Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Power, being beyond the Power and ability of all Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures; then, though you will not give credit to any bare af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firmations of my self, because I say I am the Son of God; yet believe the things for the testimony that my works give unto it. Proper effects give Testimony to the proper cause; He who doth those things which none but God can do, must needs be God, or Impowred by God to do them.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> believe the works <ns0:hi>i</ns0:hi>: that ye may know and believe <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 14, 11. and 17, 2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>, that the Father <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in me, and I in him <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">This is the way for you to know, be perswaded, and to believe, That the Father is in me by his mighty Divine working Power, Chap. 14.10. <ns0:hi>The Father that dwelleth in me, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e doth the works</ns0:hi>; and I work in, and together with him. This phrase, <ns0:hi>The Father is in me, and I in him</ns0:hi>; teacheth us three things concerning Christ. 1. His Oneness in Nature and Essence with the Father. 2. His Personal distinction from his Father; here are two mentioned, the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Me.</ns0:hi> None can properly be said to be in himsef. 3. The most perfect, and intimate<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> indwelling of one of the persons in the <ns0:hi>Holy Trinity,</ns0:hi> in the other.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.3.44. and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>3.</ns0:note> Therefore they sought again to take him <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Because he said, that the Father was in Him, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the Father; by which they well enough understood, that he asserted an union with the Father; they did not again go about to stone him, as they did before; he had sufficiently stopped their mouths, as to their imputation of Blasphe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />my; but they seek to apprehend him, with a design (no doubt) to carry him before the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim,</ns0:hi> (their great Court, which had Cognisance of those things)</ns0:note>: but he escaped out of their hand <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">But as he had once and again before, so he now again escapeth out of their hands: whether by darkning the Air before their Eyes, or (as some would have it) making his Body invisible, by his Divine Power; or what other way, the Scripture tells us not, and it is great rashness to determine.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And went away again beyond Jordan, into the place where John at first baptized <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Christs time was not yet come when he should be be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trayed, and Crucified; it was yet three months and more to it; He saw the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> were in such a rage and fury, that there was no staying in that place: He goes be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yond <ns0:hi>Iordan</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Bethabara,</ns0:hi> where he found <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> at first Baptizing, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.28. before he Baptized in <ns0:hi>Enon</ns0:hi> near <ns0:hi>Salim: Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.23. See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.28. Possibly he chose that place, as being a place where <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> had been preparing a way for him, by turning mens hearts in some measure for receiving the Gospel, and pointing out Christ to his Disciples, as the Lamb of God who taketh away the sins of the World.</ns0:note>: and there he abode <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">How long he abode there, we cannot tell; probably, till he took his last journey from <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> of which the other Evange<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ists speak, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 20.17. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 10.32. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 18.31. What he did in <ns0:hi>Galile<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> during these three months, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> reports not, onely saith,</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And many resorted unto him, and said, John did no miracle <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">God so ordered it in the Wisdom of his Providence, that though <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elisha</ns0:hi> under the Law wrought miracles, by which they confirmed their Divine Mission; yet <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> coming immediately before Christ, as his Messenger and Forerunner, wrought none<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that so the glory of Christ in working miracles when he came, might be more clear and evident. This made the People, that came to Christ while he was in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> say thus amongst themselves, We paid a great Veneration to <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the Baptist, yet he never did those things which Christ hath done.</ns0:note>: but all things that John spake of this man were true <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">And whatsoever <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> told us of this Person, hath proved true; He hath done, and doth greater things than ever <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> did: and is in the judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of sense to be preferred before him: shou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d we not now believe in him: <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> told us he was the <ns0:hi>Lamb of God,</ns0:hi> who takes away the sins of the World: and told us much more concerning him, which our Eyes see is true.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:352" />42 And many believed on him there <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Some believed on him, as such whom <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist</ns0:hi> had spoken him to be: others possibly <ns0:hi>believed on him</ns0:hi> in the sense mentioned, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 2.23. Not to the saving of their Souls, but as one sent of God, a great Prophet, no ordinary Man. The rage of men shall not hinder the progress of the Gospel.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
